title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
summary: Evaluate the expression written as a sequence of tokens.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–10,000 tokens. Each is +, − (written as ASCII '-'), *, /, or a decimal integer from −200 to 200. The expression is valid, no divisor is zero, and intermediate values and the result fit signed 32-bit integers. Division truncates toward zero.

statement: Evaluate the expression written as a sequence of tokens. Numbers appear before the operators that use them. Each operator consumes the two most recent available values, using the earlier one as its left operand. Return the integer result.

examples.explanation: Division discards the fractional part toward zero.

constraints: 1–10,000 tokens. Each is +, − (written as ASCII '-'), *, /, or a decimal integer from −200 to 200. The expression is valid, no divisor is zero, and intermediate values and the result fit signed 32-bit integers. Division truncates toward zero.
hints: Conceptual: A number can wait until an operator tells you how to use it.
Directional: Keep pending values in a stack.
Implementation: Pop the right operand first and the left operand second. Compute the result and push it back.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space for n tokens, since each token causes a constant number of stack operations.
